arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case claim the Federal Arbitration Act requires a stay that preserves court jurisdiction.
the opposing sides claim the same statute requires a stay that ends court jurisdiction.
Justice Jackson questioned whether the statutory text supports the sides that brought the case' interpretation.
Justice Sotomayor asked if a court can dismiss a case for lack of subject matter jurisdiction.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether a federal court retains jurisdiction after staying a lawsuit for arbitration. the sides that brought the case argue the court must keep control. the opposing sides argue the court must release control.
